searchText: Got it This design still has the property that if the state gets big that parts of it start getting completely forgotten, that would be really problematic right? Like for example, if two adjacent accounts A and B are in the inactive state and both get forgotten (nobody bothers storing them anymore), then it would no longer be possible to create anything between A and B in the inactive state And so if something gets created within that interval in the *active state*, then when it has to be moved, there is no way to progress the chain (to be clear, I don't think this is fatal, it's just a limitation of the statelessness schemes that I've seen so far that either you have this property that the inactive state must still be small enough to have a guarantee that _someone_ stores each part of it, or there is a risk that entire address ranges get disabled like this)
